passage.title: WORKING FROM A COWORKING SPACE
passage.subtitle: Hannah's creative office in Leeds
paragraphs: Hannah is a twenty-six-year-old graphic designer. She works for herself, so for two years she worked alone at her kitchen table. However, she started feeling lonely and found it hard to stop working in the evening.

In January, Hannah joined a shared office building called BrightDesk in the centre of Leeds. She pays a monthly fee for a desk near a big window, fast internet, and unlimited tea and coffee. There are also three quiet meeting rooms where she can talk to clients on video calls.

About forty people work at BrightDesk, including software engineers, writers and photographers. Hannah likes having colleagues around her again. During lunch breaks, she often sits in the sunny courtyard with two web developers and shares ideas about new projects.
Now, Hannah finishes work at half past five and leaves her laptop in a locker at the office. She says going home without work has made her evenings much happier and more relaxing.
